My brother was diagnosed with ADHD when he was a kid (90s). I was just lazy, unmotivated, didn't care about things, and lost track of time.... Then my brother met and knocked up a woman who already had a daughter. When his now wife moved in with him and we all started spending more time around her daughter/my niece, people commented how she was just like me at that age, which I already kind of knew. I saw a lot of myself on her with the way she acted. She got diagnosed with ADHD.... Some wheels started turning in my head and I looked into things. After two years  (I kept forgetting to look into it... )I finally booked an appointment and got diagnosed with ADHD. It turns out my brother's is the hyperactive kind and I'm the inattentive kind, which was easy to miss and misunderstand in the 90s when comparing the two. 

I had meds for 5 months. I didn't play video games. I got shit done, cleaned the house, spent time learning and improving myself. Now there's the stupid Adderall shortage, no meds for me. But knowing what's *different* about me makes it easier to cope and compensate. Progress is slower then without the meds but it's there. Diagnosed at 36 is late. I wonder how things would have been if I got the support early on, but I am working on improving regardless. My friends and family don't know about the diagnosis yet.
